newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DIHT warns against euro delays in accounts.
newsitem.headline: German DIHT warns against euro delays in accounts.

text.p: A leading German corporate lobby group said on Wednesday that the finance ministry's provisional plans to introduce the euro in the public administration at the latest possible date in 2002 would hurt German companies.

Guenter Albrecht, chief economist of the Federation of German Chambers of Industry and Commerce (DIHT), said in a radio interview that other European countries that take part in European economic and monetary union (EMU) were planning to introduce the single currency in public administration years before that.

"German companies that set up their accounts in the new currency will have to revert back to marks for tax statements and balance sheets," Albrecht told German radio. "This will be a disadvantage to companies that make early switches to the euro."
Albrecht said other countries such as Belgium and France were planning to introduce the euro in the public administration as soon as 1999.
Albrecht said he was hopeful that the finance ministry would reconsider and introduce the euro in all of the public adminstration at an early date.
